lane_title: Native WebKit Host Architecture Correction — Supersede SwiftUI Product Views with Bridge Frontend Host
supersedes_boundary: Gridline Developer Studio Shell v1 — the N0 native SwiftUI macOS application shell that rendered typed developer-workflow projection states across 5 native product views (Connect, Repository Estate, Project Studio, Inference Studio, Publish Preview).
supersession_authority: User-directed architectural revision. N0 was truthfully implemented and published for the earlier product interpretation. The production architecture is now clarified: Rig Relay is a native macOS host application that embeds the existing bridge-powered web frontend in WKWebView, not a SwiftUI-rendered product UI.

upstream_commits_verified.n0: f59caadf / 3451609e — Gridline Developer Studio Shell v1, published and audited, now architecturally superseded
upstream_commits_verified.e0: published — Frontend Systems Atlas, three-surface architecture

corrected_architecture.product_surface: The actual product UI is the bridge-powered web frontend (frontend/desktop/ — 57 files of vanilla HTML/CSS/JS, with a Redux-style runtime kernel, WebSocket transport, projection rendering, chat, widgets, and notifications). This frontend has already received design and debugging investment.
corrected_architecture.host_role: The macOS application is a thin native host that embeds the bridge frontend in a WKWebView. SwiftUI provides: native chrome (window chrome, menus), loading/failure/bootstrap/extension-status surfaces, native capability prompts, and app lifecycle management.
corrected_architecture.swiftui_product_views: N0's 5 native product views (ConnectView, RepositoryEstateView, ProjectStudioView, InferenceStudioView, PublishPreviewView) are no longer the production rendering boundary. They are demoted to non-production Reference/ fixtures preserved for migration reference.
corrected_architecture.frontend_hosting: The production app launches a WKWebView loading the bridge frontend (from the DesktopBridgeServer at https://127.0.0.1:<port>/). A typed NativeMessageBridge provides frontend-to-host and host-to-frontend message transport for native-only capabilities.
corrected_architecture.safari_extension_contract: A typed native-app messaging endpoint contract is published for Lane Q0 consumption. The contract defines message envelope, extension-origin validation, and supported initial intents. Actual Safari extension implementation belongs to Q0.

released_boundary: Native WebKit Host v1 — a thin native macOS application that: (1) opens the product through a WKWebView-hosted bridge frontend loaded from a trusted app origin; (2) restricts navigation to trusted origins only; (3) provides a typed frontend-to-native and native-to-frontend host message contract for native-only capabilities; (4) renders only boot/loading, frontend-load-failed, bridge-unavailable, unsupported-navigation-refusal, extension-status, and native-permission/status surfaces in SwiftUI; (5) exposes a typed native-app Safari extension messaging endpoint contract for Q0 consumption; (6) performs no GitHub, AgentLoop, context-assembly, local-inference, Pages-publication, or evidence-authority work in host code.
stated_consumer_purpose: A developer launches the macOS application and sees the real bridge frontend (not duplicate SwiftUI product views). The frontend communicates with the Python backend via existing WebSocket protocol. Native-only capabilities (file dialogs, keychain, extension status) route through the typed host message bridge. Q0 can consume the published native extension contract to build the Safari Web Extension feature surface.
deferred_seams: Live Safari Web Extension feature implementation (Lane Q0)
Bridge frontend bootstrap compatibility verification with WKWebView host (may need P0 coordination)
XCTest harness for WKWebView message handling
Full accessibility audit for the host shell
